clue.text: Without locks, so in an anxious state

definitions.meaning: read playfully as DIS- plus a word for having tresses, i.e. stripped of one's hair

explanation.walkthrough: The first definition is whimsical: 'dis-' as an undoing prefix plus 'tressed' (having tresses, or locks of hair) suggests someone with their hair removed.
explanation.definitionFit: The playful sense is someone deprived of their hair; the ordinary sense is someone upset, worried or suffering anguish.

clue.text: Speed, causing dismay

definitions.meaning: a rush or sprint, as in making a quick run
to dishearten, as when hopes are crushed

explanation.definitionFit: A sprint is a quick run, and to crush someone's hopes is to dishearten them, both senses of the same short word.

clue.text: Pottery shop carrying a new variety

indicators.note: a shop that carries goods holds something within it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a store is a shop

indicators.note: a new variety suggests the letters of the words a new in a different arrangement

explanation.surface: A crockery shop stocks a fresh range of goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variety' scrambles A NEW into NEWA before 'carrying' puts it inside the shop.
explanation.definitionFit: Stoneware is a dense, hard-fired kind of ceramic ware, so it is one type of pottery.

clue.text: Equestrian appendage

definitions.meaning: a clause added to a document or bill

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a person on horseback; the other is a clause tacked onto a legal document or parliamentary bill.

clue.text: One of the family goes ahead

parts.note: steps means goes, walks
on means ahead, onward, as in go on

explanation.surface: A relative pushes forward in front of the others.
explanation.definitionFit: A spouse's son from an earlier marriage is a member of the household by remarriage.

clue.text: Slip out in time to write a letter tea Greek

annotationWithheld.clue: Slip out in time to write a letter tea Greek

clue.text: No back-handed honour!

parts.note: a token of victory that is also the inner face of the hand, which is the opposite of its back

explanation.walkthrough: A palm leaf was a token of victory (to bear the palm), and the palm of the hand is the inner face, the opposite side from the back.
explanation.definitionFit: The victor's prize is a frond worn in triumph, and the same word names the inner face of the hand rather than its back.

clue.text: Unsuitable for a girl

parts.note: miss is a young woman or girl

explanation.surface: Something is not right for a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Something wrong or out of order is improper, inappropriate, unsuitable.

clue.text: Well he won't exert himself

parts.note: someone in perfectly good health who still refuses to work, feigning illness

explanation.walkthrough: 'Well' looks like an interjection opening a sentence, but it means in good health: the shirker pretends to be ill.
explanation.definitionFit: A shirker feigns sickness to avoid duty, so although healthy they do no work.

clue.text: Corrupted, but decent if refer med

indicators.note: reformed means formed again, so the letters of the words decent if are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone tainted who could become decent if they changed their ways.
explanation.walkthrough: The scanned text splits the anagram signal into two pieces; read as one word it means formed anew.
explanation.definitionFit: Tainted or contaminated, as a wound or computer file can be, is a sense of corrupted.

clue.text: Bore could not get a seat

definitions.meaning: remained upright for lack of a chair

explanation.definitionFit: To bear something is to tolerate it, and passengers with no chair remained on their feet.

clue.text: 13 tail off, and that's characteristic

parts.note: the answer to 13-across, the German city in the Ruhr

indicators.note: off means wrong or awry, so the letters of tail are rearranged

explanation.surface: A city's tail goes off, which is typical.
explanation.walkthrough: '13' points to the answer to 13-across; 'off' turns TAIL into TIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: An essential quality is intrinsic, fundamental to the nature of a thing, so it is characteristic of it.

clue.text: It's true accepting proportional representation is giving satisfaction

indicators.note: something accepting another thing takes it in, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: real means genuine, true
PR is the standard abbreviation for proportional representation, an electoral system

explanation.surface: A voting reformer argues that a fairer electoral system brings contentment.
explanation.walkthrough: Satisfaction here is the old sense of redress for a wrong, as in demanding satisfaction in a duel; 'accepting' puts PR and IS inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Retaliation is taking revenge for an injury, the redress once called satisfaction, so it is a noun phrase sense of giving redress.

clue.text: German city acquiring French art with foreign money

parts.note: es is French for 'art' as in 'thou art', the verb
a sen is a small coin of Japan and other Asian countries

explanation.surface: A city in Germany buys French paintings with overseas cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'art' is not painting but the old verb form 'thou art', which in French is 'tu es'.
explanation.definitionFit: Essen is an industrial city in the Ruhr region of Germany.

clue.text: A feeling for the right technique following study

indicators.note: following means the second word comes after the first in the answer

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
science means skill or technique, as in the science of boxing

explanation.surface: A sense of what is correct comes once you have learnt the method.
explanation.definitionFit: The moral sense that tells right from wrong is an inner feeling guiding behaviour.

clue.text: Too vain maybe to get much applause

indicators.note: maybe suggests a possible version of the words too vain, rearranged

explanation.surface: A performer is too conceited to receive a standing reception.
explanation.definitionFit: Sustained, enthusiastic clapping from an audience is a standing tribute.

clue.text: Nomination in brief

parts.note: a name shortened to its first letters, a naming given in abbreviated form

explanation.definitionFit: The first letters of someone's names are their name given in short form.

clue.text: Striking appears ineffective

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits the word into two: NOT ABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Remarkable things stand out, and read as two words the answer means incapable.

clue.text: A person who finds work telling

definitions.text: A person who finds work telling

parts.words: A person who finds work telling
parts.note: a bank employee at the counter is called a teller, so their work is telling in a different sense from being significant

explanation.walkthrough: 'telling' looks like 'significant' or 'revealing', but it is the job of a teller, who counts out money at a bank counter.
explanation.definitionFit: A cashier in a bank is a teller, whose daily work is counting out money.

clue.text: Observe the top man can be trying!

parts.note: to see is to observe
a king is the man at the top of a kingdom

explanation.surface: Watching the boss can be wearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trying' looks like an adjective meaning tiresome, but it is the participle of try, as in trying to find.
explanation.definitionFit: Looking for or attempting something, as in trying to do it, is searching.

clue.text: Rotten ingrate so hard

indicators.note: rotten means spoilt or decayed, so the letters of ingrate are reworked

explanation.surface: A thankless person is so unfeeling.
explanation.definitionFit: A very tough igneous rock, often used figuratively for something unyielding and hard.

clue.text: An Italian writer-somewhat slow

parts.note: Dante Alighieri, the Italian poet who wrote the Divine Comedy

explanation.surface: An Italian author is a bit sluggish.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical tempo marking meaning at a moderate walking pace, rather slow.

clue.text: Individual charging a spender about two hundred

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece is placed round the other

parts.note: a user is one who uses up or consumes, a spender
CC is two hundred in Roman numerals, C being one hundred

explanation.surface: A big spender running up two hundred is charged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the two hundred inside A plus the spender; a user consumes or spends resources.
explanation.definitionFit: One who brings a charge against someone is a person making an accusation.

clue.text: Old people confined to bed want nice nightwear

indicators.note: confined to says the letters are held inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Elderly folk stuck in bed would like attractive pyjamas.
explanation.walkthrough: The Iceni were an ancient British tribe led by Boudicca against the Romans.
explanation.definitionFit: A tribe of ancient Britain is a people from long ago.

clue.text: Young swimmer always to be seen around lake

indicators.note: around means the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: ever means always
L is the standard abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: A youngster in the pool is constantly found near the lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A young eel is a fish in its early stage, so a young swimmer.

clue.text: Soundness of article about clerical employment

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
C is short for circa, Latin for about
a curacy is the office of a curate, a junior priest

explanation.surface: An essay on a priest's job asks how sound it is.
explanation.definitionFit: Correctness and precision are what make an argument sound.

clue.text: To agitate could mean gaol!

explanation.definitionFit: To rouse or mix is one sense; the other is British slang for jail, as in doing time.

clue.text: Newfangled ideas come out even in fiction

parts.note: a novel is a work of fiction
ties means draws, finishes level

explanation.surface: Fresh concepts emerge in a work of fiction.
explanation.definitionFit: New and unusual things or ideas are innovations.

clue.text: Ocean-going vessels moving quickly

explanation.definitionFit: A navy's group of ships at sea, and an adjective meaning swift.

clue.text: A person entitled to order real change

indicators.note: change says the letters of real are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone with a title demands real reform.
explanation.definitionFit: A British nobleman ranking above a viscount holds a title, so he is literally entitled.

clue.text: This is enough to make one weep!

definitions.text: This is enough to make one weep!

parts.words: This is enough to make one weep!
parts.note: a sentimental film or story designed to bring on crying

explanation.definitionFit: A sentimental film or book designed to make audiences cry.
